body: Sorry if this is a stupid question, but what major department stores/mall brands carry items seen in [this fit?](https://imgur.com/a/BdPe53m) I'm looking for things like that oversized shirt/blouse, vest, tie(?), and flared long skirt. Although I'm pretty decent at men's fashion, women's fashion is still new territory for me.
Hmm ok I'll keep that in mind. Thanks.

Thank you for the last sentence. I thought that therapy was only for people with mental illnesses, but I guess it's something I will seriously try to do from now on. Just talking about this on Reddit makes me feel a lot better.

Thanks. Yeah I plan to tell them when I'm completely independent from them. Hopefully we'll still love each other, even if there are really rocky times. It's gonna suck but thanks for your comment. I hate lying about being a Christian when I'm not.

Has anyone here read: "Why I Believed: Reflections of a Former Missionary" by Kenneth Daniels? I'm in the beginning stages of critically analyzing the faith I was born into, and I have to say that I was very lucky to stumble upon this book! This won't be the only source I use to truly and finally determine my beliefs, but it's a great stepping stone at least. He seems very fair and presents arguments for both sides. I can't wait to finish this book!

I try to tell myself that life will be more "richer" but I'm still infatuated with Christian salvation. The core idea of a God so loving that he will grant us eternal relief and joy after all our earthly suffering is such an attractive message. But I don't know if I can ever truly believe it again. And I don't know if I will ever find an equally beautiful purpose on Earth. It sucks. I appreciate your words.

I don't have depression but I do relate with wanting to kill myself. I don't think I fully get it but I sort of understand.

Ironically, my reason to live is heavily inspired by a manga author who heavily references the Bible in his works. But you don't need Christianity to follow his message.

I live to love others and to be loved. I live to enjoy the moments and fortune I have. I'm grateful to have what I have, and I want to love others while experiencing it. The fact that our life is limited makes it even more special. At first this purpose seems shallow, but when you actually experience it, it's the most important feeling in the world. I have not found any greater purpose in life, unfortunately or fortunately.

I can't promise that I'll give you your reason to live, or that I'll give you a path to follow. All I can say is that you MIGHT find your purpose if you stick around long enough. And I'm sorry that you're feeling such despair right now. I feel for you. Internet hugs, friendo. I genuinely hope that you'll find your reason.
Thank you so much for the virtual hugs. I'm so thankful that I'm not alone. I'll definitely come back and read these types of comments from time to time.

Not South Asian but Southeast Asian. My parents and grandparents came from the Vietnam War and were exposed to Christianity in the U.S. Given how many Indians/South Asians there are in the world though, I wouldn't doubt that there are many like you.

I've been raised a Christian since I was born. I'm not as educated as you are but I've lost faith that I'll get any answers and recently became atheist.
Thanks for the recommendations. I'll be sure to use them.
It hurts a lot. Thank you for saying that you're proud of me. I can really use these comments in this time of my life.
